alt: Pakistan Studies 0448 has two papers: Paper 1, History and Culture, and Paper 2, the Environment of Pakistan. In Paper 2, Section 1, the Land of Pakistan, sits at the base, supporting Section 2 on natural resources and the later sections, which use its places, ranges and rivers without re-explaining them.
caption: Learn Section 1 first: the rest of Paper 2 builds on it.

after: ## Location (1a–1b): what candidates must be able to do on a map
alt: A schematic grid of the reference lines for Section 1(a): latitudes 30°N and 36°N, the Tropic of Cancer further south, and longitudes 64°E, 70°E and 76°E, with the Arabian Sea to the south.
caption: Six lines frame Pakistan’s position: learn them before placing any feature.

after: ## Location (1a–1b): what candidates must be able to do on a map
alt: The fifteen named cities from Islamabad to Gwadar as a checklist. Gilgit, Chitral, Gwadar and Hyderabad are highlighted with the two common mistakes: placing Gilgit or Chitral too far south, and confusing coastal Gwadar with inland Hyderabad.
caption: Place cities relative to each other; watch the northern and coastal ones.

alt: A schematic, not a map. The Hindu Kush, Karakoram and Himalaya form an arc across the north to north-east; the Balochistan Plateau and Sulaiman Range lie to the west; the Potwar Plateau and Salt Range are in the north-centre. The Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi and Sutlej feed the Indus. Safed Koh, the Kabul, Hab and Dasht rivers and the Thar, Thal and Kharan deserts are also named.
caption: Learn landforms by position: northern arc, west, north-centre, then the Indus system.

alt: Three climate features with a benefit and a problem for each: monsoon rain supports agriculture but flooding disrupts industry and communications; cold in the mountains constrains lives but feeds the glacial meltwater that sustains the Indus; drought and water shortage harm agriculture and industry.
caption: Pair every climate benefit with a problem to reach the top marks.

alt: Three stacked layers of one outline map: first administrative areas and cities, then landforms and rivers, then a simple climate-zone overlay. A note says to revisit the map whenever later Paper 2 topics mention a Section 1 place.
caption: Build one map in three layers and keep returning to it.
